questions.q: How does A* typically outperform Dijkstra while still finding the same optimal path?
options: It uses a heuristic — an estimate of remaining distance to the target — to prioritize exploring paths heading toward the target, rather than expanding uniformly in every direction
It skips checking some nodes entirely, sacrificing correctness for speed

A* and Dijkstra always explore exactly the same number of nodes
questions.explain: A* uses a heuristic (e.g. straight-line distance) to focus its search, typically exploring far fewer nodes than Dijkstra's uniform outward expansion.
